t3.CLAIM: T3 — Wall-Clock Exposure Invariance on Event-Clock Covariates
t3.MECHANISM: An event-count survival clock stretches apparent duration in quiet sessions; exact wall-clock (t_start, t_stop] exposure should decouple trade-arrival seasonality from time-in-state.
t3.TEST: Identical Cox baseline hazards under wall-clock vs event-count exposure, unstratified and hour-of-day stratified, on BTCUSDT aggTrades event-clock spells with purged CPCV and macro censoring.
t3.KILL LINE: Under wall-clock exposure, trades/min significant at p<0.01 after HOD stratification, OR HOD stratification shifts HRs outside unstratified 95% CIs.
t3.STATUS: tested-fail — KILL: under wall-clock exposure, raw trade-arrival density remains significant after HOD stratification (HR=0.9998, p=4.67e-42 < 0.01) — dead mechanism: event-count exposure conflates arrival sparsity with survival duration
t3.WHAT IT CANNOT TELL YOU: Whether true liquidity aging operates in physical vs event time once full incremental L2 book updates arrive.
t3.DATA FLAG: DATA FLAG: aggTrades = taker-side executed prints only; no resting quote additions/cancellations, no queue depth, no iceberg visibility. All features in this run are TAKER-ONLY.
